kin.form: 猿田彦 (Sarutahiko), 'Monkey-Field Prince,' kami of crossroads and guidance

kin.label: Domain

pronunciation.note: Sarutahiko is Tier 2: plain Hepburn. He is the kami who guided Ninigi's descent and who stands at boundaries.

domains.title: Monkey-Field Prince
domains.subtitle: Guide of the Heavenly Descent, Guardian of Crossroads
domains.lead: Sarutahiko is the kami who stands at the boundary between heaven and earth. When Ninigi descended from Takamagahara, Sarutahiko blocked the way until Ame-no-Uzume persuaded him to become the guide. With his long nose, glaring eyes, and red face, he became the model for the taikomochi and tenjin figures of Japanese folk performance and the patron of those who stand at thresholds.

cards.name: Guide of Ninigi
cards.desc: He led Ninigi's descent from heaven to earth.

cards.name: Crossroads Guardian
cards.desc: He protects boundaries, paths, and transitions.

cards.name: Husband of Uzume
cards.desc: Ame-no-Uzume married him after negotiating the heavenly descent.

cards.name: Folk Performer
cards.desc: His appearance influenced comedic and ceremonial performers.

mythology.lead: Sarutahiko's mythology centers on the moment when the heavenly line met the earthly kami and found a guide rather than an enemy.

myths.title: The Blockade at the Heavenly Bridge
myths.text: When Ninigi prepared to descend from heaven, the earthly kami Sarutahiko stood at the Floating Bridge of Heaven and refused passage. None of the heavenly envoys could persuade him. Finally Ame-no-Uzume, the goddess of dance and laughter, went forward. She exposed herself and made him laugh, then convinced him to submit and guide Ninigi's descent.

myths.title: Marriage to Ame-no-Uzume
myths.text: After guiding Ninigi, Sarutahiko married Ame-no-Uzume. Their union symbolized the alliance between heavenly and earthly powers and the role of humor and persuasion in resolving cosmic standoffs.

myths.title: Patron of Performers and Boundaries
myths.text: Sarutahiko's grotesque and powerful appearance made him a patron of street performers, comedians, and those who manage transitions. His image appears at festival processions and at shrines dedicated to safe travel and guidance.

lore.syncretism: Sarutahiko is an earthly kami who becomes an ally of the heavenly order. His long nose and red face connect him to other boundary figures in Japanese folk religion, and his marriage to Ame-no-Uzume unites two of the most dynamic kami in the pantheon. He is also venerated in Shugendō as a guide for mountain ascetics.
lore.culturalLegacy: Sarutahiko is worshipped at Tsubaki Grand Shrine and other shrines associated with guidance and performance. His image influences Japanese masks, festival costumes, and the design of tenjin figures. He remains the kami you call upon when standing at a threshold.
lore.extendedMeditation: Sarutahiko stands at the edge of two worlds. He is not an enemy of heaven but its necessary guide: the one who knows the way down. His marriage to Uzume reminds us that the most stubborn boundaries can be crossed with courage, humor, and respect.

sources.name: Bocking, A Popular Dictionary of Shinto

lore.archaeology: Tsubaki Grand Shrine in Mie is the head shrine of Sarutahiko. The iconography of crossroads and boundary kami is preserved in shrine statuary, festival costumes, and pilgrimage markers across Japan.
